text:
Anna Chen: quick design pass — rule stack ordering feels ambiguous when multiple rules share the same priority. screenshot: https://img.redwood.dev/ux/stack-order.png
Mike R: agree. the drag handle visuals overlap the adjacent item, so it’s unclear which will become active when you drop
Sophia Patel: idea — show a translucent ghost placeholder where the item will land + a match-count pill in the left gutter so you can see impact while dragging :bulb:
Derek Li: also we need better inline validation copy. current 'invalid rule' is too vague for users to fix conflicts
Anna Chen: suggested copy: "Rule conflict: multiple rules would match the same input. Reorder to resolve or refine the conditions." Short and actionable
Jin (designbot): a11y notes — announce "drag started" and "position X of Y" via aria-live while reordering. ensure reorder handle is keyboard focusable and exposes up/down actions
Mike R: quick validation example for engs — current API returns something like:
```
{
  "error": "conflict",
  "message": "2 rules match incoming request. Reorder or refine the conditions.",
  "affected_rules": ["rule-73", "rule-74"]
}
```
Sophia Patel: Preview simulator quirk: after editing conditions our sim sometimes shows 0 matches even when sample traffic should match. feels like it’s using cached saved rules not the draft. propose a "Run simulation (draft)" toggle and a small "results stale" banner when the draft differs from saved config
Derek Li: +1. Also show a small spinner and disable Run while the simulator compiles the new route set. show sample input carousel so product can eyeball why a rule matched or not
Anna Chen: copy tweak for the button: change label from "Run sim" to "Run simulation (draft)" and tooltip: "Simulate using current unsaved edits". should reduce confusion
Mike R: :thumbsup: I can do a tiny PR for the button label and tooltip. will also add match-count pill in the gutter per Sophia
Derek Li: i'll pick up the aria-live announcements and keyboard reordering semantics. will add notes in the accessibility doc
Sophia Patel: i'll refine the validation copy and write a short playbook: "how to resolve conflict" with screenshots and step-by-step reorder flow
Anna Chen: plan: Mike -> label + match-count + ghost placeholder visuals, Derek -> a11y hooks, Sophia -> copy + playbook. we’ll demo tomorrow at 10am. thanks everyone :rocket:
